title: Why All World Maps Are Wrong
speaker: Vox
description: Every world map you've seen is wrong — but in different ways. Vox explains why it's mathematically impossible to flatten a sphere without distortion, and how different map projections warp size, shape, and distance.

title: Gerrymandering: How Politicians Rig Elections
speaker: Vox
description: Politicians can legally choose their own voters — and it's called gerrymandering. Vox explains how district lines are drawn to favor one party, why it's so hard to stop, and what a fair map would actually look like.

title: Why Cities Are Full of Uncomfortable Benches
speaker: Vox
description: Why do park benches have armrests in the middle? Why are doorways spiked? Vox explores 'hostile architecture' — the intentional design of public spaces to exclude homeless people — and what it says about who cities are built for.

title: The Man Who Rigged America's Election Maps
speaker: Vox
description: How did one political operative redraw the maps of an entire country to lock in partisan power for a decade? Vox investigates the story of Thomas Hofeller — the architect of modern gerrymandering — and the documents he left behind.

title: How the US Made Affordable Homes Illegal
speaker: Vox
description: America has a housing shortage — and zoning laws are a big reason why. Vox explains how local rules made affordable, dense housing illegal in most neighborhoods, and why this drives up costs and inequality.

title: The Real Reason American Health Care Is So Expensive
speaker: Vox
description: The US spends more on healthcare than any country on Earth — but why? Vox breaks down the structural reasons behind America's uniquely expensive medical system, and why simply switching to single-payer wouldn't fix it.

title: The Big Debate About the Future of Work, Explained
speaker: Vox
description: Will robots take our jobs? Economists and futurists disagree sharply about how automation will reshape work — with some predicting mass unemployment and others expecting adaptation. Vox maps out both sides of the debate.

title: How America Became a Superpower
speaker: Vox
description: In just 200 years, the US went from a small coastal republic to the world's dominant superpower. Vox traces the history of American expansion — from westward conquest to world wars — and asks what it means to be a superpower today.

title: The Roots of America's Democracy Problem
speaker: Vox
description: America's political system is increasingly giving minority-rule outcomes — where the party with fewer votes wins power. Vox explains the structural features of US democracy that make this possible, and what reformers want to change.
